---
title: "A First Example"
---

In this exercise, you'll give 13 prompts to a coding agent and watch what it does with a short R script. The goal is to get a feel for the workflow and to make sure the software works on your machine. You'll see one run of each prompt. In lecture, we'll look at what happens across many runs.

The script, `logit.R`, is supposed to print a predicted probability from a logit model. It has two bugs.

## Before you start

Install your model and interface first ([Choose your setup](setup.qmd)). Then install the R and git tools below.

You'll use three programs. Run R code in RStudio. Run the agent in the terminal (Terminal on a Mac, PowerShell on Windows). Look at what the agent changed in GitHub Desktop (or with git in the terminal).

## The exercise

{{< include _partials/_part0.md >}}

### How to run each prompt

Run the prompts in order. Most of them come in pairs: a short version of a
request, then a more careful version of the same request. Start a fresh
session for every prompt, so the agent remembers nothing from the last one.

Click your setup.

::: {.panel-tabset group="pair"}

## Claude Code + Claude

Claude Code sends the contents of the files it reads to Anthropic. So never
start an agent in a folder that holds restricted or identifiable data. (The
folder for this exercise holds only simulated data.)

1. Make sure the *Changes* tab in GitHub Desktop lists no files.
2. In the terminal, start Claude Code from inside the folder:

   ```sh
   cd ~/Documents/GitHub/agentic-ai-example
   claude --model haiku --permission-mode manual
   ```

3. Paste the prompt. In this mode, Claude Code asks before it runs a command
   or edits a file. Read each request, since it shows what the agent is about
   to do. Then choose *Yes*. Don't choose the option that tells it not to ask
   again.
4. Write down about how long the reply took and what it says.
5. Quit with `/exit`.
6. Look at the *Changes* tab, write down which files changed, and discard the
   changes.

Each reply takes about 5 to 20 seconds, plus the time you take to read the
requests.

## Claude Code + qwen

Never start an agent in a folder that holds restricted or identifiable data.
(The folder for this exercise holds only simulated data.)

Make sure Ollama is running (its icon is in the menu bar on a Mac or the
system tray on Windows).

1. Make sure the *Changes* tab in GitHub Desktop lists no files.
2. In the terminal, start Claude Code from inside the folder:

   ```sh
   cd ~/Documents/GitHub/agentic-ai-example
   ollama launch claude --model qwen3-coder:30b --yes -- --permission-mode manual
   ```

3. Paste the prompt. In this mode, Claude Code asks before it runs a command
   or edits a file. Read each request, since it shows what the agent is about
   to do. Then choose *Yes*. Don't choose the option that tells it not to ask
   again.
4. Write down about how long the reply took and what it says.
5. Quit with `/exit`.
6. Look at the *Changes* tab, write down which files changed, and discard the
   changes.

[CTK: how long a reply takes with Claude Code and qwen; not yet timed.]
Sometimes the model writes out a tool call as text instead of running it, and
the reply stops there. If that happens, write it down as a run that failed and
go on to the next prompt.

## OpenCode + qwen

Never start an agent in a folder that holds restricted or identifiable data.
(The folder for this exercise holds only simulated data.)

Make sure Ollama is running (its icon is in the menu bar on a Mac or the
system tray on Windows).

1. Make sure the *Changes* tab in GitHub Desktop lists no files.
2. In the terminal, start OpenCode from inside the folder:

   ```sh
   cd ~/Documents/GitHub/agentic-ai-example
   opencode --model ollama/qwen3-coder:30b
   ```

3. Stay in **Build** mode (the footer says "Build"). In Build mode, OpenCode
   runs commands and edits files without asking. Plan mode, which the Tab key
   switches to, is read-only, and the model then refuses to run R. Paste the
   prompt.
4. Write down about how long the reply took and what it says.
5. Quit with `ctrl+c`.
6. Look at the *Changes* tab, write down which files changed, and discard the
   changes.

Each reply takes about one to five minutes. Sometimes the model writes out a
tool call as text (e.g., `<function=read>`) instead of running it, and the
reply stops there. If that happens, write it down as a run that failed and go
on to the next prompt.

## OpenCode + gpt-oss

Never start an agent in a folder that holds restricted or identifiable data.
(The folder for this exercise holds only simulated data.)

Make sure Ollama is running (its icon is in the menu bar on a Mac or the
system tray on Windows).

1. Make sure the *Changes* tab in GitHub Desktop lists no files.
2. In the terminal, start OpenCode from inside the folder:

   ```sh
   cd ~/Documents/GitHub/agentic-ai-example
   opencode --model ollama/gpt-oss:20b
   ```

3. Stay in **Build** mode (the footer says "Build"). In Build mode, OpenCode
   runs commands and edits files without asking. Plan mode, which the Tab key
   switches to, is read-only, and the model then refuses to run R. Paste the
   prompt.
4. Write down about how long the reply took and what it says.
5. Quit with `ctrl+c`.
6. Look at the *Changes* tab, write down which files changed, and discard the
   changes.

Each reply takes about 15 seconds to a minute on a computer with 32 GB of
memory, and longer on a computer with 16 GB. Sometimes the model writes out a
tool call as text instead of running it, and the reply stops there. If that
happens, write it down as a run that failed and go on to the next prompt.

### Clean up

In GitHub Desktop, click *Repository* > *Remove...*, check the box that also
moves the repository to the Trash (the Recycle Bin on Windows), and click
*Remove*.

This leaves your model and interface installed. If you used a local model,
`ollama rm qwen3-coder:30b` or `ollama rm gpt-oss:20b` frees the space it uses.
